direction.premise: Players secretly legislate how autonomous game pieces act around one royal throne.
direction.composition: A two-column stone council on desktop: carved board and law ledger, with the active hand underneath. Mobile prioritizes board and own cards, then ledger.
direction.shapeLanguage: Architectural cuts, carved borders, engraved counters, parchment rectangle decrees and slender bronze rules; every object is DOM/CSS.
direction.surfaceAndMaterial: Layered CSS gradients imply weathered limestone and paper without imported illustrations or sprites.
direction.paletteLogic: Blue North and red South champion counters, bronze high priority actions, neutral slate/ivory text.
direction.typography: Cormorant-style medieval serif headings with readable sans-serif rules and statuses, falling back to installed fonts offline.
direction.signature: Large grid throne with stamped Cyrillic role counters; read law description beneath an immediately selectable decree.
direction.distinction: Focused royal ledger and stamped law cards rather than generic floating cards, neon or game screenshots.

architecture.primaryVerb: Select an illustrated decree from your own hand, seal it, then read the combined law and shared board consequence.
architecture.physicalFeedback: A selected card is marked immediately; after both choices the round advances and the new public state persists.
architecture.spatialRationale: The shared royal board is followed by the current laws and a hand of selectable illustrated decree cards. This keeps the current game object and its real inputs spatially connected on a phone.

production.renderer: HTML/CSS only for gameplay; no PNG sprites, SVG icons or canvas art.
production.focalAsset: Code-drawn board. Separately authored 96x96 PNG icon serves only the shell/PWA.

motion.character: Selected decrees lift and brighten; active tokens travel using correct per-cell pixel deltas.
motion.action: Touch a card, read its rule in the preview, confirm law.
motion.anticipation: Selection is explicit; the confirmation stays disabled until a card is chosen.
motion.response: Turn progression remains controlled by the same game engine and PocketNet.
motion.followThrough: New turn and logs remain in view.
motion.interruption: Reduced-motion keeps the board static and preserves state.

evidence.expectedChange: An autonomous board and a five-card hand appear
